root_idea.summary: The root has two established semantic orientations: coming upon or gaining awareness of something, and raising or producing dust.
root_idea.development: The lexical tradition connects stumbling and discovery through encountering or inspecting what caused the stumble, while separately preserving the dust-and-trace branch. The Quran uses the first orientation for discovery and making something known.

qac_form_accounting.reason: Displayed under the normalized Form I citation headword عَثَرَ; the Quranic token is its passive perfect form.
Displayed under the normalized Form IV perfect citation headword أَعْثَرَ.

senses.definition: To be discovered or become known; to come upon knowledge of something.
senses.usage_conditions: In the Quranic passive construction عُثِرَ عَلَى, the matter becomes known or is discovered, characteristically without deliberate seeking.

senses.definition: To make someone discover or become aware of something; to disclose or make known to them.
senses.usage_conditions: The Quranic construction أَعْثَرَ عَلَى expresses causing others to discover or learn of something without their having sought it.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To stumble, trip, or fall, especially falling forward or upon the face.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The basic physical verb; it is used of a person or animal and may be followed by فِي for stumbling on or over something.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To stumble or falter in speech.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A figurative extension of physical stumbling, including halting, hesitating, or faltering of the tongue.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To lie or speak falsely.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A figurative usage attested in the expression العَثْرِ وَالبَائِنِ.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To enter suddenly or unexpectedly upon an affair or situation.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A figurative usage describing an unexpected encounter with an affair on which another had not entered.

other_classical_meanings.definition: For one's fortune or good fortune to fall or decline.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A figurative expression likening failing fortune to a person who has stumbled or fallen.

other_classical_meanings.definition: For a vein to pulse.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A specialized bodily usage.

other_classical_meanings.definition: For time or fortune to destroy people or cause them to be overcome.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: An idiomatic figurative construction in which time or circumstance brings about ruin or defeat.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To cause someone to stumble, trip, or fall.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The causative Form IV physical usage; it may also mean causing someone to fall prostrate.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To impugn someone's character before an authority and seek his downfall.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A figurative causative construction used with an authority or ruler.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To cause someone's fortune or good fortune to fall.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A causative figurative expression derived from the physical notion of making someone fall.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To guide or show someone the way to other people.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A causative directional usage distinct from simply causing someone to discover information.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To raise dust, earth, or small pieces of dry clay by the extremities of the toes while walking.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A specialized Form Q.Q usage associated with the dust raised by walking.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To see or behold something and identify or single it out.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The verb may describe seeing an object or individuating it by observation.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To observe birds, including seeing their movement and taking an omen from it.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A conventional bird-observation and augury construction.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A lie or falsehood.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A nominal usage separate from the verb meaning “to lie.”

other_classical_meanings.definition: A stumble or trip while walking or proceeding.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The noun also has a regular plural عَثَرَاتٌ.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A slip, lapse, fault, wrong action, or mistake.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A figurative noun for falling into error, sin, or wrongdoing.

other_classical_meanings.definition: War or fighting.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A figurative conventional usage in which warfare is treated as an occasion of stumbling; the cited expression advises not beginning hostilities.

other_classical_meanings.definition: High land without herbage and covered with dust.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A specialized geographical noun, associated with عِثْيَر dust.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Watered by rain alone or by water flowing over the surface of the ground.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Used especially of palm trees or crops receiving natural rainwater or runoff rather than deliberate irrigation.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Unoccupied or not engaged in seeking the affairs of this world or the next.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A figurative adjectival usage; جَاءَ فُلَانٌ عَثَرِيًّا means that he came unoccupied.

other_classical_meanings.definition: One who stumbles, trips, and falls often.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: An intensive or habitual characterization of a person who frequently stumbles.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Dust, especially dust that rises or spreads.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A noun synonymous with غُبَارٌ, عَجَاجٌ, or تُرَابٌ in the cited descriptions.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Dust, clay, or compact earth turned over by the extremities of the feet while walking.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The expression may refer to the disturbed earth left without a clear ordinary footprint.

other_classical_meanings.definition: An obscure or barely discernible trace or mark.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: It may be contrasted with أَثَرٌ as a less conspicuous trace; some reported explanations extend the expression to bodily form, but the core attested sense is an obscure trace.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A land containing much dust.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: An adjectival or descriptive usage applied to land.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Stumbling or tripping; one who stumbles.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: An active-participial or adjectival usage derived from the physical sense of عَثَرَ.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A liar.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A figurative adjectival usage.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Failing or fallen, said of fortune or good fortune.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The expression جَدٌّ عَاثِرٌ characterizes fortune as being in a falling state.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A hunter's snare.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: This sense is reported in an interpretation of the plural عَوَاثِرُ.

other_classical_meanings.definition: An accident or calamity that destroys a person or causes him to be overcome.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: This meaning is reported as the sense of the related feminine noun underlying one interpretation of عَوَاثِرُ.

other_classical_meanings.definition: The substance or bodily form of a thing.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A concrete noun synonymous in this usage with عَيْنٌ or شَخْصٌ.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A pit, trap, or other thing prepared to make an animal or person fall; a thing by which one is made to stumble and fall.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Its primary description is a pit dug to catch a lion or another animal; it may also denote a bark-made snare.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A cause or place of perdition or death; something perilous or destructive.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A figurative extension of the trap meaning, including use as an epithet for something perilous or destructive.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Difficulty, distress, or evil.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The expression عَاثُورُ شَرٍّ describes falling into confusion, evil, or hardship.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A channel dug to irrigate a palm tree.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A specialized agricultural usage concerning a naturally or surface-watered palm.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A well.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A separately reported concrete noun usage.

cautions: The Quranic Form I token is passive, while the public headword is normalized to the Form I dictionary citation form عَثَرَ.
The proposed eagle meaning associated with عُثْرٌ is explicitly identified in the evidence as erroneous and is not treated as a lexical meaning of this root.
